sdf_intersect — 3D sdf_csg op

• Data kinds: sdf × sdf → sdf

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.sdf_intersect(a, b) (to call the implementation directly, import sdf_ops; sdf_ops.sdf_intersect(a, b); from the registry, ops3d.get("sdf_intersect"))

Usage

The intersection of two SDFs, A∩B = the element-wise max(a, b) (inside only where both are inside).

The zero isosurface is the intersection of both boundaries. Exact SDF outside, conservative lower bound inside.

Computation: np.maximum(np.asarray(a, float64), np.asarray(b, float64)). Being an element-wise max, a point is inside A∩B (negative) only when a < 0 and b < 0. The shapes only need to be broadcast-compatible (otherwise numpy raises ValueError), and nothing else is checked. NaN propagates, ±inf propagates exactly (max(a, -inf) = a).

Input: 2 SDFs evaluated on the same grid (outputs of sphere_sdf / box_sdf / esdf etc., negative inside, positive outside). The distance unit is that of the input.

Returns: float64 of the broadcast shape. <= 0 is the occupancy of A∩B.

Notes:

• The outside value can come out smaller than the true distance: outside the intersection, when the point is outside A and outside B, max(a, b) is the distance "to the farther surface", and the surface of A∩B may be farther than that (lower bound). The zero isosurface is exact.

• If there is no common part, every element is positive (occupancy 0); this is not an error.

• Used for CSG "cut-outs", such as trimming a sphere with a box or building a prism from 2 boxes. Removing B from A is sdf_subtract.
